items.title: Smooth and K-finite vectors for SL2(R), and the (g,K)-module
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $G=\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb R)$, $K=\mathrm{SO}(2)$ with the rotation parameter $k_\theta$, and $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb R)$ with complexification $\mathfrak g_\mathbb C=\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)$ ([[def-iwasawa-and-minimal-parabolic-data-for-sl2-r]], [[def-special-linear-lie-algebra-sl-two]]). For a strongly continuous unitary representation $(\pi,H)$, define smooth vectors by norm-smoothness of the orbit map and $K$-finite vectors by finite-dimensional $K$-orbit span; put $V=H^{\infty,K}$ ([[def-strongly-continuous-unitary-representation]]). For real $X$ define $L_Xv=\frac{d}{dt}|_{t=0}\pi(\exp_G(tX))v$ on $H^\infty$ and extend complex-linearly ([[def-one-parameter-subgroup-of-a-lie-group]], [[thm-one-parameter-subgroups-are-exactly-exponentials]]). The operators preserve $H^\infty$, form a Lie-algebra action under the tangent bracket, and extend uniquely to a unital $U(\mathfrak g_\mathbb C)$-action ([[def-lie-bracket-on-the-tangent-space-of-a-lie-group]], [[def-universal-enveloping-algebra-as-a-tensor-quotient]], [[prop-lie-algebra-actions-extend-to-unital-actions-of-the-enveloping-algebra]]). With $W=-i\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\-1&0\end{pmatrix}$ and $E_\pm=\frac12\left(\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}\pm i\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}\right)$, set $H_n=\{v:\pi(k_\theta)v=e^{in\theta}v\text{ for all }\theta\}$ and $V_n=V\cap H_n$. The Casimir from [[def-quadratic-casimir-element]] is $\Omega=\tfrac18W^2-\tfrac14W+\tfrac12E_+E_-\in Z(U(\mathfrak g_\mathbb C))$, as follows from its Killing-dual basis; it is central by [[prop-the-quadratic-casimir-element-is-central]].

items.title: Smooth and K-finite vectors are dense and stable under the derived action
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and fix a left Haar measure $dg$ on $G=\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb R)$ for the integrated form of [[def-integrated-form-of-a-unitary-representation]]. Let $(\pi,H)$ be a strongly continuous unitary representation of $G=\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb R)$ ([[def-strongly-continuous-unitary-representation]]), with smooth vectors $H^\infty$ and $V=H^{\infty,K}$ as in [[def-k-finite-and-smooth-vectors-for-sl2-r]]. Then:

**(1)** $H^\infty$ is dense in $H$ and is stable under every derived operator $L_X$; the resulting $U(\mathfrak g_\mathbb C)$-module structure is the one defined in [[def-k-finite-and-smooth-vectors-for-sl2-r]].

**(2)** $V$ is dense in $H$, and $H=\widehat\bigoplus_{n\in\mathbb Z}H_n$ with $H_n=\{v:\pi(k_\theta)v=e^{in\theta}v\}$ the $K$-isotypic spaces.

**(3)** Every nonzero closed $\pi(G)$-invariant subspace $M\subseteq H$ satisfies $M\cap V\ne\{0\}$.

**(4)** $V=\bigoplus_{n\in\mathbb Z}V_n$ is stable under $\mathfrak g_\mathbb C$ and $K$, and the $U(\mathfrak g_\mathbb C)$-action on $H^\infty$ restricts to $V$; in particular, the enveloping-algebra element $XY$ acts as $L_XL_Y$ for $X,Y\in\mathfrak g_\mathbb C$.

If $H=\{0\}$, the density and direct-sum statements are trivial and no nonzero invariant subspace occurs.
items.strategy:
**(1)** In an identity neighborhood $U$, construct a nonnegative smooth compactly supported function in the explicit determinant-one matrix chart and normalize its Haar integral to one, using positivity on open sets and finiteness on compact sets ([[def-left-haar-integral-and-left-haar-measure]], [[lem-haar-measure-is-positive-on-nonempty-open-sets-and-finite-on-compact-sets]]). For $f\in C_c^\infty(G)$, set $f_h(x)=f(h^{-1}x)$. Left Haar invariance and the weak integrated-form identity give $\pi(h)\pi(f)=\pi(f_h)$; a common compact support and uniform continuity of parameter derivatives show $h\mapsto f_h$ is $C^\infty$ in $L^1$, while $\|\pi(q)\|\le\|q\|_1$. Thus $\pi(f)v$ is smooth. Strong continuity and the mass-one kernels give $\|\pi(f_U)v-v\|\to0$, proving density of $H^\infty$. Its derived operators and $U$-module structure are supplied by [[def-k-finite-and-smooth-vectors-for-sl2-r]].

**(2)** Every irreducible unitary representation of $K=\mathrm{SO}(2)$ is finite dimensional by the compact-group decomposition theorem. Since $K$ is abelian, Schur's lemma makes each group operator scalar, so irreducibility forces dimension one. A continuous character $q(\theta)$ is smooth under AC_\omega; differentiating its homomorphism law gives $q(\theta)=e^{ia\theta}$, and $2\pi$-periodicity forces $a\in\mathbb Z$. Thus the irreducibles are exactly $\chi_n(k_\theta)=e^{in\theta}$. The compact-group decomposition and isotypic-projection suppliers then identify $H$ with the Hilbert sum of the $H_n$ and provide projections $P_n$. For smooth $w$, differentiate $\pi(g)P_nw=\int_K\overline{\chi_n(k)}\pi(gk)w\,dk$ under the compact integral, using the Bochner norm inequality and uniform convergence of derivative difference quotients; hence $P_nw\in V$. Finite partial sums of $P_nw$ approximate each smooth $w$, proving $V$ dense. A finite-dimensional $K$-orbit span decomposes into finitely many of these characters, giving $V=\bigoplus_nV_n$.

**(3)** For nonzero $v\in M$, choose $U$ so $\sup_{g\in U}\|\pi(g)v-v\|<\|v\|/2$. The mass-one kernel gives a smooth $w=\pi(f_U)v$ with $\|w-v\|<\|v\|/2$, so $w\ne0$; pairing against $M^\perp$ shows $w\in(M^\perp)^\perp=M$. The Hilbert sum has some $P_nw\ne0$, and the smoothness and invariant-subspace preservation of $P_n$ from (2) give a nonzero vector of $M\cap V$.

**(4)** Smooth orbit maps stay smooth under right translation. For $v\in V$, $k\mapsto\pi(k)v$ has finite-dimensional span and $\pi(k)L_Xv=L_{\operatorname{Ad}(k)X}\pi(k)v$; expanding $\operatorname{Ad}(k)X$ and $\pi(k)v$ in finite bases shows the orbit of $L_Xv$ also has finite-dimensional span. Thus $V$ is $K$- and $\mathfrak g_\mathbb C$-stable, and the enveloping-algebra action restricts. The zero-Hilbert-space and empty nonzero-subspace cases are as stated. AC is used through the Haar/Riesz integrated form, compact-group decomposition and projections, and AC_\omega in the automatic-smoothness supplier. Kowalski's Lemma 7.4.8 is a model-specific analogue on $H_\chi$; the general assertions here are proved directly.

items.title: Highest- and lowest-weight submodules at the exceptional parameters
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix $\varepsilon\in\{0,1\}$ and $
u\in\mathbb C$, and let $I^K_{\varepsilon,
u}$ be the compact-picture $(\mathfrak g,K)$-module with K-type basis $f_m(k_	heta)=e^{im	heta}$ for $m\equiv\varepsilon\pmod2$ from [[lem-k-type-decomposition-of-the-sl2-principal-series]]. Use the compact-picture action of [[thm-compact-picture-of-the-sl2-principal-series]] and the basis $J,H,S,W,E_\pm$ and Casimir $\Omega$ normalized in [[def-k-finite-and-smooth-vectors-for-sl2-r]]. For real $X$, write $L_Xf=\left. rac{d}{dt}ight|_{0}\Pi_
u(\exp_G(tX))f$, and extend complex-linearly. Let $\mathcal W_\varepsilon=\{
u\in\mathbb Z:
u\equiv\varepsilon+1\pmod2\}$ from [[def-normalized-principal-series-i-epsilon-nu]].

**(a)** Let $n\in\mathcal W_\varepsilon$, $n\ge1$. Inside $I^K_{\varepsilon,n}$ set $M^-_{n+1}:= igoplus_{j\ge0}\mathbb Cf_{n+1+2j}$ and $M^+_{-(n+1)}:= igoplus_{j\ge0}\mathbb Cf_{-(n+1)-2j}$. Then $L_{E_-}f_{n+1}=0$, $L_{E_+}f_{-(n+1)}=0$, $M^+_{-(n+1)}$ is an irreducible highest-weight submodule of highest weight $-(n+1)$, and $M^-_{n+1}$ is an irreducible lowest-weight submodule of lowest weight $n+1$. Their direct sum is the unique maximal proper submodule, and the quotient is the finite-dimensional simple module $L_{n-1}$ with K-types $n-1,n-3,\dots,-(n-1)$ and dimension $n$.

**(b)** Let $n\in\mathbb Z$, $n\ge2$, and $
u=n-1\in\mathcal W_\varepsilon$. Then $M^+_{-n}:= igoplus_{j\ge0}\mathbb Cf_{-n-2j}$ is an irreducible highest-weight submodule of highest weight $-n$, and $M^-_n:= igoplus_{j\ge0}\mathbb Cf_{n+2j}$ is an irreducible lowest-weight submodule of lowest weight $n$. The Casimir $\Omega$ acts on both by $	frac18((n-1)^2-1)$.

**(c)** For $\varepsilon=1$ and $
u=0$, one has $I^K_{1,0}=M^-_1\oplus M^+_{-1}$, where $M^-_1= igoplus_{j\ge0}\mathbb Cf_{1+2j}$ and $M^+_{-1}= igoplus_{j\ge0}\mathbb Cf_{-1-2j}$ are the irreducible lowest- and highest-weight submodules, respectively. The Casimir acts on $I^K_{1,0}$ by $-	frac18$.
items.strategy:
**(1)** Differentiate the exact compact-picture cocycle locally along the explicit one-parameter subgroups for J,H,S. The bottom row of k_theta exp(sX) determines the Iwasawa height and angle; its norm and angular derivatives yield L_J, L_H, L_S and then the fixed L_E± ladder coefficients. Verify their sl2 commutators on the basis, so the Casimir polynomial acts through the resulting enveloping-algebra action.

**(2)** A K-stable submodule splits into its f_m weight lines by averaging each finite K-orbit span against e^{-im theta}. At nu=n the only boundary zeros are L_E- f_{n+1}=0 and L_E+ f_{-(n+1)}=0; the two tails are invariant and irreducible. The quotient has the n central weights n-1,n-3,...,-(n-1); all internal ladder coefficients are nonzero, making it a simple highest-weight module L_{n-1}. Any proper submodule therefore lies in the tail sum, which is the unique maximal proper submodule.

**(3)** At nu=n-1 the zeros are at f_n and f_{-n}, giving the stated irreducible tails. At epsilon=1, nu=0 the odd K-types split at f_1 and f_{-1} into the two limit modules. Finally, from the normalized Casimir Omega=W^2/8-W/4+E_+E_-/2 and the local coefficients, Omega f_m=(nu^2-1)f_m/8. AC supplies normalized Haar probability for K-averaging.

items.title: Holomorphic and antiholomorphic discrete-series models
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $\mathfrak H=\{z\in\mathbb C:\operatorname{Im}z>0\}$ be the upper half-plane ([[def-unit-disc-upper-half-plane-and-blaschke-factor]]) with the action $g\cdot z=\frac{az+b}{cz+d}$ of $g=\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{pmatrix}\in\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb R)$ and automorphy factor $j(g,z)=cz+d$ ([[def-modular-group-action-on-the-upper-half-plane]], [[def-mobius-transformation]]). For an integer $n\ge2$ put
$$\mathcal H_n^+=\Big\{f:\mathfrak H\to\mathbb C\ \text{holomorphic}:\ \|f\|_n^2=\int_{\mathfrak H}|f(z)|^2y^{\,n-2}\,dx\,dy<\infty\Big\},\qquad y=\operatorname{Im}z,$$
and let $\mathcal H_n^-$ be the complex-conjugate space of antiholomorphic functions with the same norm. Define
$$\pi_n(g)f(z)=j(g^{-1},z)^{-n}f(g^{-1}\cdot z),\qquad \pi_n^-(g)f=\overline{\pi_n(g)\bar f};$$
the verification below proves these are group actions preserving the stated finite-norm spaces. For $j\ge0$, set
$$f_{n,j}(z)=(z-i)^j(z+i)^{-n-j}\in\mathcal H_n^+,\qquad \pi_n(k_\theta)f_{n,j}=e^{-i(n+2j)\theta}f_{n,j},$$
and set $\widetilde f_{n,j}=\overline{f_{n,j}}\in\mathcal H_n^-$, so that $\pi_n^-(k_\theta)\widetilde f_{n,j}=e^{i(n+2j)\theta}\widetilde f_{n,j}$. Let $V_n^-:=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb C}\{f_{n,j}:j\ge0\}$ and $V_n^+:=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb C}\{\widetilde f_{n,j}:j\ge0\}$. The models are denoted $D_n^-:=(\pi_n,\mathcal H_n^+)$ and $D_n^+:=(\pi_n^-,\mathcal H_n^-)$. For the parity $\varepsilon\equiv n\pmod2$, the displayed algebraic K-finite subspaces identify with $M^+_{-n}$ and $M^-_n$ in [[lem-highest-and-lowest-weight-submodules-at-principal-series-reducibility-points]](b), at $\nu=n-1$.
items.strategy: Define the inverse-weighted action and verify its cocycle law and norm preservation by change of variables. Use the Cayley coordinate to prove the displayed vectors have finite positive norm and compute their K-weights. The disk realization makes these vectors smooth; direct differentiation gives the ladder operators, which match the extremal principal-series modules at ν=n−1 with ε≡n (mod 2).

items.title: The weighted discrete-series space is a Hilbert space with K-type basis
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). In the notation of [[def-holomorphic-and-antiholomorphic-discrete-series-models]], for every integer $n\ge2$:

**(1)** $\mathcal H_n^+$ is a complex Hilbert space with inner product $\langle f,h\rangle_n=\int_{\mathfrak H}f\bar h\,y^{n-2}dx\,dy$, and point evaluations $f\mapsto f(z)$ are bounded, uniformly on compact subsets of $\mathfrak H$.

**(2)** The vectors $f_{n,j}$, $j\ge0$, are nonzero, mutually orthogonal, and have finite norm; their closed linear span is $\mathcal H_n^+$. The action of $K$ on this Hilbert space is strongly continuous and its irreducible K-types are exactly the one-dimensional lines $\mathbb C f_{n,j}$ with characters $\chi_j(k_\theta)=e^{-i(n+2j)\theta}$, each with multiplicity one. The analogous statements hold for $\mathcal H_n^-$ with $\widetilde f_{n,j}$ and characters $e^{i(n+2j)\theta}$.

**(3)** For $j\ge0$, the corresponding isotypic projection is the Bochner integral
$$P_jf=\int_K\chi_j(k)^{-1}\pi_n(k)f\,dk,$$
where $dk$ is normalized Haar probability; every $f\in\mathcal H_n^+$ is the orthogonal sum $f=\sum_{j\ge0}P_jf$ in Hilbert norm.
items.strategy: Prove point evaluation bounds by the Cauchy mean-value inequality, then show the holomorphic space is closed in weighted L2. The Cayley map turns the norm into a radial weighted disk norm; Taylor coefficients and monotone convergence give the complete orthogonal monomial expansion. Use that dense expansion to establish strong continuity on K, then apply compact-group decomposition and evaluate the character projections.

items.title: The weighted area form is SL2(R)-invariant
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). In the notation of [[def-holomorphic-and-antiholomorphic-discrete-series-models]], for every integer $n\ge2$ and $g\in G=\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb R)$:

**(1)** The weighted density attached to the model action is invariant: for every $f\in\mathcal H_n^+$, the change of variables $z=g\cdot w$ gives
$$|\pi_n(g)f(z)|^2(\operatorname{Im}z)^{n-2}dx_zdy_z=|f(w)|^2(\operatorname{Im}w)^{n-2}dx_wdy_w$$
after pullback. Thus $\pi_n(g)$ is a bijective linear isometry of $\mathcal H_n^+$, and $\pi_n$ is a unitary representation on this Hilbert space; the conjugate action $\pi_n^-$ is also unitary.

**(2)** These unitary representations are strongly continuous on $G$.
items.strategy: Differentiate the fractional-linear map to compute its real Jacobian, combine it with the upper-half-plane imaginary-part identity and the automorphy cocycle, and apply nonnegative C1 change of variables to prove norm invariance. The group law and inverse come from the model action. Strong continuity follows from the dense smooth vector span and the isometry estimate.

items.title: Irreducibility and K-types of the discrete series
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). For every integer $n\ge2$, the representations $D_n^-=(\pi_n,\mathcal H_n^+)$ and $D_n^+=(\pi_n^-,\mathcal H_n^-)$ of $G=\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb R)$ are irreducible strongly continuous unitary representations. Their K-type decompositions are
$$\mathcal H_n^+=\overline{\bigoplus_{j\ge0}\mathbb C f_{n,j}},\qquad \pi_n(k_\theta)f_{n,j}=e^{-i(n+2j)\theta}f_{n,j},\qquad \mathcal H_n^-=\overline{\bigoplus_{j\ge0}\mathbb C\widetilde f_{n,j}},\qquad \pi_n^-(k_\theta)\widetilde f_{n,j}=e^{i(n+2j)\theta}\widetilde f_{n,j},$$
each character occurring with multiplicity one. The displayed algebraic K-finite subspaces $V_n^-,V_n^+$ of [[def-holomorphic-and-antiholomorphic-discrete-series-models]] are isomorphic as $(\mathfrak g,K)$-modules to $M^+_{-n}$ and $M^-_n$, the extremal submodules of [[lem-highest-and-lowest-weight-submodules-at-principal-series-reducibility-points]](b) at $\nu=n-1$; in particular, the Casimir $\Omega$ of [[def-k-finite-and-smooth-vectors-for-sl2-r]] acts on these algebraic modules by $\tfrac18((n-1)^2-1)$.
items.strategy: Use the complete K-type expansion and character projections to obtain a K-type vector in any nonzero closed invariant subspace. The smooth model vectors have nonzero raising and lowering coefficients, so the subspace contains every K-type; density gives irreducibility. The local model-module identification transfers the extremal labels and Casimir.

items.title: The two limits of discrete series
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). In the compact picture of the normalized principal series ([[def-normalized-principal-series-i-epsilon-nu]], [[thm-compact-picture-of-the-sl2-principal-series]]), let $I_{1,0}$ act on $L^2_1(K)=\{f\in L^2(K):f(k_{\theta+\pi})=-f(k_\theta)\}$. Its K-finite vectors are $\bigoplus_{m\text{ odd}}\mathbb C f_m$ ([[lem-k-type-decomposition-of-the-sl2-principal-series]]). Define
$$M^-_1:=\bigoplus_{j\ge0}\mathbb C f_{1+2j},\qquad M^+_{-1}:=\bigoplus_{j\ge0}\mathbb C f_{-1-2j},$$
and let
$$D^-_1:=\overline{M^+_{-1}},\qquad D^+_1:=\overline{M^-_1}$$
in $L^2_1(K)$. The two limits of discrete series are the resulting closed summands: $D^-_1\oplus D^+_1=L^2_1(K)$ orthogonally, with K-types $e^{-i(1+2j)\theta}$ and $e^{i(1+2j)\theta}$ respectively, each with multiplicity one. The K-finite modules are $(\mathfrak g,K)$-submodules, with $L_{E_-}f_1=L_{E_+}f_{-1}=0$; the Casimir $\Omega$ acts on these algebraic modules by $-\tfrac18$ ([[lem-highest-and-lowest-weight-submodules-at-principal-series-reducibility-points]](c)).

For every $n\ge2$, the discrete-series modules $M^+_{-n}$ and $M^-_n$ at $\nu=n-1$ are the algebraic K-finite spans in the holomorphic and antiholomorphic models $D^-_n,D^+_n$ ([[def-holomorphic-and-antiholomorphic-discrete-series-models]](b)). At the formal endpoint $n=1$, the candidate $q_1(z)=(z+i)^{-1}$ has infinite weighted norm $\int_{\mathfrak H}|q_1(z)|^2y^{-1}dx\,dy$, so this endpoint is realized inside $I_{1,0}$ and not by a finite-norm holomorphic model.
items.strategy: Use the compact-picture unitarity and odd K-type basis to define positive and negative tail closures. The local exceptional-parameter lemma gives their algebraic ladder actions and Casimir, and the K-type supplier gives orthogonality and density. The unfinished principal-series unitarity supplier is the open input for G-invariance of the closures. Prove the formal n=1 holomorphic candidate has divergent weighted norm directly.

items.title: KAK integration formula for K-bi-invariant functions on SL2(R)
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and use the conventions of [[def-iwasawa-and-minimal-parabolic-data-for-sl2-r]]. Fix the left Haar measure $dg$ of [[thm-iwasawa-decomposition-for-sl2-r]], so in NAK coordinates it is $e^{-s}\,dx\,ds\,dk$ with normalized Haar probability $dk$ on $K$. Write $a_t=\operatorname{diag}(e^{t/2},e^{-t/2})$ for $t\ge0$.

For every continuous nonnegative $K$-bi-invariant function $\psi:G\to[0,\infty)$, the following equality holds for extended nonnegative integrals:
$$\int_G\psi(g)\,dg=2\pi\int_0^\infty\psi(a_t)\sinh(t)\,dt.$$

Consequently, for every continuous complex-valued $K$-bi-invariant function $\varphi$ and $p\in\{1,2\}$,
$$\int_G|\varphi(g)|^p\,dg=2\pi\int_0^\infty|\varphi(a_t)|^p\sinh(t)\,dt,$$
with extended values; thus $\varphi\in L^p(G)$ exactly when the radial integral is finite. If $\varphi\in L^1(G)$, the same formula holds for the absolutely convergent complex integral of $\varphi$. More generally, if $\varphi$ is continuous and satisfies $\varphi(k_1gk_2)=\chi_1(k_1)\chi_2(k_2)\varphi(g)$ for continuous unitary characters $\chi_i:K\to S^1$, then $|\varphi|$ is $K$-bi-invariant and the same $L^1$ and $L^2$ criteria apply.
items.strategy:
**(1)** For $g\in G$, diagonalize the positive matrix $g^Tg$ with an oriented orthonormal eigenbasis. Its positive eigenvalues have product one, giving $g=k_1a_tk_2$ with $t\ge0$; $\operatorname{tr}(g^Tg)=2\cosh t$ makes $t$ unique ([[cor-real-spectral-theorem-for-self-adjoint-endomorphisms]]).

**(2)** Insert the fixed NAK Haar formula from [[thm-iwasawa-decomposition-for-sl2-r]]. For $g=n_xa_s$, put $y=e^s$ and use the Cayley radius $r=2\operatorname{artanh}|(x+i(y-1))/(x+i(y+1))|$. Direct trace and modulus calculations show this is the unique KAK parameter, while $e^{-s}ds=dy/y^2$.

**(3)** The inverse Cayley map changes $dx\,dy/y^2$ to $4\,du\,dv/(1-|w|^2)^2$. Polar coordinates $w=\rho e^{i\theta}$ and the nonnegative C1 change-of-variables theorem give $\sinh r\,dr\,d\theta$; integrating the full angle contributes $2\pi$. The theorem's AC_omega hypothesis is supplied by AC ([[thm-c-one-change-of-variables-for-nonnegative-lebesgue-measurable-functions]], [[lem-ac-supplies-countable-and-dependent-choice-for-banach-integration]]).

**(4)** Apply the extended identity to $|\varphi|$ and $|\varphi|^2$ for the $L^1$ and $L^2$ criteria; when $\varphi\in L^1$, decompose its real and imaginary parts into positive and negative parts to obtain the complex integral formula. For continuous unitary-character covariance, $|\varphi|$ is bi-invariant.

items.title: Matrix-coefficient formulas and decay for the discrete and principal series
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

**(a) Discrete series.** Let $n\ge2$, let $u_n=f_{n,0}/\|f_{n,0}\|_n\in D_n^-$ be the normalized extremal vector of [[def-holomorphic-and-antiholomorphic-discrete-series-models]], and let $c_n(g)=\langle\pi_n(g)u_n,u_n\rangle$ be its matrix coefficient ([[def-matrix-coefficient-of-a-unitary-representation]]). Then for all $\tau\in\mathbb R$,
$$c_n(a_\tau)=\cosh(\tau/2)^{-n}.$$
Moreover, for every $X,Y\in U(\mathfrak g_{\mathbb C})$ there is $C=C(n,X,Y)>0$ such that
$$\bigl|\langle\pi_n(g)Xu_n,Yu_n\rangle\bigr|\le C\,e^{-n|\tau|/2}\qquad(g=k_1a_\tau k_2).$$

**(b) Limits and unitary principal series.** In the compact picture of $I_{1,0}$ ([[thm-compact-picture-of-the-sl2-principal-series]], [[thm-unitarity-of-the-sl2-unitary-principal-series]], [[def-limits-of-discrete-series-for-sl2-r]]), let $\Pi_0$ be the unitary action on $L^2_1(K)$ and $f_1(k_\theta)=e^{i\theta}$ the normalized weight-one vector. Then
$$\langle\Pi_0(a_\tau)f_1,f_1\rangle=\operatorname{sech}(\tau/2)=\frac{2}{e^{\tau/2}+e^{-\tau/2}}.$$
Consequently $\int_0^\infty|\langle\Pi_0(a_\tau)f_1,f_1\rangle|^2\sinh\tau\,d\tau=+\infty$, and this matrix coefficient is not in $L^2(G)$ by the KAK formula ([[lem-kak-integration-formula-for-k-bi-invariant-functions-on-sl2-r]]).

More generally, for every odd integer $m$ and every real spectral parameter $s$, let $c_{m,s}(\tau)=\langle\Pi_{is}(a_\tau)f_m,f_m\rangle$ in the unitary compact picture of $I_{1,is}$. Then for an absolute constant $C>0$,
$$|c_{m,s}(\tau)|\le C(1+|\tau|)e^{-|\tau|/2}\qquad(\tau\in\mathbb R).$$
items.strategy: Compute the discrete-series action in the Cayley disk coordinate: every fixed K-type coefficient is cosh^{-n} times a polynomial in tanh, and finite enveloping-algebra vectors yield the same radial decay. In the unitary compact picture, the Iwasawa cocycle gives an absolute coefficient bound by an elementary angular integral, while direct angular integration gives the exact weight-one limit coefficient and KAK proves it is not square-integrable.

items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $n\ge2$ and let $D_n^-=(\pi_n,\mathcal H_n^+)$ and $D_n^+=(\pi_n^-,\mathcal H_n^-)$ be the holomorphic and antiholomorphic discrete-series models of [[def-holomorphic-and-antiholomorphic-discrete-series-models]]. Every matrix coefficient $g\mapsto\langle\pi_n(g)v,w\rangle$ with $v,w$ K-finite belongs to $L^2(G)$ for the fixed Haar measure in [[lem-kak-integration-formula-for-k-bi-invariant-functions-on-sl2-r]], for each of $D_n^-$ and $D_n^+$. Moreover, each of $D_n^-$ and $D_n^+$ is unitarily equivalent to a closed $G$-invariant subspace of the left regular representation $\lambda$ on $L^2(G)$ ([[def-left-and-right-regular-unitary-representations]]).
items.strategy: For K-finite vectors, use the explicit disk-coordinate coefficient polynomials from [[lem-k-type-coefficient-formulas-for-the-sl2-discrete-and-principal-series]] and the KAK formula of [[lem-kak-integration-formula-for-k-bi-invariant-functions-on-sl2-r]] to bound every coefficient by $C_{v,w}e^{-n|t|/2}$ and integrate. To embed $D_n^-$ in the left regular representation, define $\Phi(v)(g)=\langle\pi_n(g^{-1})v,e_0\rangle$ for the normalized extremal vector $e_0$. The explicit $e_j,e_0$ coefficient and the weighted disk norm show that all $\Phi(e_j)$ have the same squared L2 norm $4\pi/(n-1)$; their distinct left K characters make them orthogonal. Thus $\Phi$ extends, after scaling, to an isometry on the Hilbert completion. Identify the extension with the coefficient almost everywhere by [[cor-l-p-convergent-sequences-have-almost-everywhere-convergent-subsequences]], which proves the intertwining identity with the left regular action. Complex conjugation gives the antiholomorphic embedding and coefficient result.

items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). The two limits $D_1^-,D_1^+$ of [[def-limits-of-discrete-series-for-sl2-r]] are irreducible strongly continuous unitary representations of $G=\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb R)$, with multiplicity-one K-type chains of weights $-(1+2j)$ and $+(1+2j)$, respectively, and Casimir scalar $-\tfrac18$. They are the orthogonal direct summands of the unitary principal series $I_{1,0}$: $$I_{1,0}=D_1^-\oplus D_1^+.$$
items.strategy: At the odd endpoint, the compact-picture theorem supplies the strongly continuous unitary action and its explicit Iwasawa cocycle. The cocycle makes each K-character vector analytic along the two unipotent one-parameter subgroups; the exceptional ladder coefficients keep all Taylor coefficients in the same one-sided tail, proving the closed limits are G-invariant. Compact K-character projections then isolate a nonzero weight in any nonzero closed invariant subspace, and the nonzero internal ladder arrows generate the whole chain, proving irreducibility. The limit definition supplies the orthogonal Hilbert-space split, while the extremal module lemma supplies the weights and Casimir. The compact-picture supplier remains open pending its Step-3 reconciliation.

items.title: The limits of discrete series are not square-integrable
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Define a square-integrable irreducible unitary representation to mean one for which every matrix coefficient lies in $L^2(G)$; this is the discrete-series convention of Frahm's SL$(2,\mathbb R)$ Plancherel notes. Let $D_1^-$ and $D_1^+$ be the two limits of discrete series of [[def-limits-of-discrete-series-for-sl2-r]]. Neither is square-integrable. In the compact picture of $I_{1,0}$, the normalized weight-one vector $f_1(k_\theta)=e^{i\theta}$ in $D_1^+$ has coefficient
$$\langle\Pi_0(a_\tau)f_1,f_1\rangle=\operatorname{sech}(\tau/2),\qquad a_\tau=\operatorname{diag}(e^{\tau/2},e^{-\tau/2}),$$
and
$$\int_G|\langle\Pi_0(g)f_1,f_1\rangle|^2\,dg=2\pi\int_0^\infty\operatorname{sech}^2(\tau/2)\sinh\tau\,d\tau=+\infty.$$
Complex conjugation gives the same nonintegrable coefficient modulus on $D_1^-$. This statement establishes failure of the all-coefficients criterion; it makes no claim about Plancherel support or occurrence in the regular representation.
items.strategy: Use [[lem-k-type-coefficient-formulas-for-the-sl2-discrete-and-principal-series]](b) for the normalized weight-one coefficient in $D_1^+$ and the KAK identity of [[lem-kak-integration-formula-for-k-bi-invariant-functions-on-sl2-r]] to compute its full Haar integral. The radial integrand is exactly $2\tanh(\tau/2)$, so the integral diverges. In the compact picture at parameter zero, the action is real under pointwise complex conjugation; conjugation carries the positive limit chain to the negative one, giving the same non-L2 coefficient modulus on $D_1^-$. This proves failure of the all-coefficients definition of square-integrability and makes no Plancherel-support assertion.

items.title: Tempered unitary representations
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $G$ be a locally compact, $\sigma$-compact group with a fixed left Haar measure, and let $\lambda_G$ be its left regular representation on $L^2(G)$ ([[def-left-and-right-regular-unitary-representations]], [[thm-regular-representations-are-unitary-and-strongly-continuous]]). A strongly continuous unitary representation $\pi$ of $G$ is **tempered** if it is weakly contained in $\lambda_G$ ([[def-strongly-continuous-unitary-representation]], [[def-weak-containment-of-unitary-representations]]); explicitly, each continuous positive-type coefficient $g\mapsto\langle\pi(g)\xi,\xi\rangle$ is approximable uniformly on compact subsets of $G$ by finite sums of positive-type coefficients of $\lambda_G$. The **reduced (tempered) dual** is $\widehat G_{\mathrm{red}}:=\{[\sigma]\in\widehat G:\sigma\prec\lambda_G\}$, the Fell support of the regular representation ([[def-fell-topology-on-the-unitary-dual]], [[def-unitary-dual-of-a-locally-compact-group]]). Thus an irreducible unitary representation is tempered exactly when its equivalence class is a point of $\widehat G_{\mathrm{red}}$. A reducible representation may be tempered by the same weak-containment condition, but it is not itself a point of the irreducible unitary dual.
items.strategy: Definition: weak containment is the compact-uniform positive-type coefficient condition. For an irreducible representation its class lies in the reduced dual exactly when it is weakly contained in the regular representation; reducible representations are tempered by the same condition but are not points of the irreducible dual. AC is inherited through the Haar-based regular representation and the set/Fell constructions of the unitary dual; weak containment itself adds no choice.

items.title: Classification of the irreducible unitary dual of SL2(R)
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $G=\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb R)$ and let $\widehat G$ be its irreducible unitary dual. Every irreducible strongly continuous unitary representation of $G$ is unitarily equivalent to exactly one member of the following list:

**(i)** the trivial representation;

**(ii)** a unitary principal series $I_{\varepsilon,i\nu}$ with $\varepsilon\in\{0,1\}$ and $\nu\ge0$, excluding $(\varepsilon,\nu)=(1,0)$. The parameter identification is $I_{\varepsilon,i\nu}\cong I_{\varepsilon,-i\nu}$, proved below by the phase-normalized ladder intertwiner.

**(iii)** a discrete series $D_n^+$ or $D_n^-$, $n\ge2$, whose K-finite module is respectively $M_n^-$ or $M_{-n}^+$ at exceptional parameter $n-1$ ([[thm-irreducibility-and-k-types-of-the-discrete-series]]).

**(iv)** one of the two limits $D_1^+$ or $D_1^-$; they are the irreducible summands in $I_{1,0}\cong D_1^+\oplus D_1^-$ ([[thm-unitarity-and-irreducibility-of-the-limits-of-discrete-series]]). Thus the reducible $I_{1,0}$ is not itself a point of $\widehat G$.

**(v)** a spherical complementary series $I_{0,\nu}$ with $0<\nu<1$.

For every irreducible $\pi$ on $H_\pi$, the image $\pi(C^*(G))$ contains $\mathcal K(H_\pi)$. Consequently $C^*(G)$ is GCR, $G$ is type I, and the Mackey and Fell-topology Borel structures on $\widehat G$ agree and are standard; the planned batch-1 supplier for the last two clauses is `lem-gcr-kernel-and-mackey-borel-characterizations`, whose item file is not yet present ([[def-full-group-c-star-algebra]], [[def-type-i-factor-representation-and-type-i-group]], [[def-unitary-dual-of-a-locally-compact-group]], [[def-fell-topology-on-the-unitary-dual]]).

Classify the resulting unitary ladder strings by positivity and endpoints, and prove the global model intertwiners by a Banach-valued Taylor bound with radius uniform in the orbit center. The type-I and Borel conclusion uses the batch-1 separability and GCR criteria, whose statements, Mackey Borel prerequisite, and type-I interface remain unfinished and are explicitly held.

items.title: Fell continuity of the unitary principal series in the parameter
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $G=\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb R)$, $\varepsilon\in\{0,1\}$, and $s_0\in\mathbb R$. Write $H_\varepsilon=L^2_\varepsilon(K)$ and let $\Pi_{\varepsilon,s}$ be the compact-picture representation of $I_{\varepsilon,is}$ on $H_\varepsilon$ ([[thm-compact-picture-of-the-sl2-principal-series]]). For every $\xi\in H_\varepsilon$ and compact $Q\subseteq G$,
$$\sup_{g\in Q}\left|\langle\Pi_{\varepsilon,s}(g)\xi,\xi\rangle-\langle\Pi_{\varepsilon,s_0}(g)\xi,\xi\rangle\right|\longrightarrow0\qquad(s\to s_0).$$
For $\delta>0$, set $J_{\varepsilon,s_0,\delta}=\{s\in\mathbb R:0<|s-s_0|<\delta,\ (\varepsilon,s)\ne(1,0)\}$ and $S_{\varepsilon,s_0,\delta}=\{[I_{\varepsilon,is}]:s\in J_{\varepsilon,s_0,\delta}\}\subseteq\widehat G$ ([[thm-generic-irreducibility-and-the-exceptional-parameter-lattice]]). Then $\Pi_{\varepsilon,s_0}$ is weakly contained both in the parameter-indexed direct sum $\widehat{\bigoplus}_{s\in J_{\varepsilon,s_0,\delta}}\Pi_{\varepsilon,s}$ and in the direct sum of one representative of each class in $S_{\varepsilon,s_0,\delta}$ ([[def-weak-containment-of-unitary-representations]], [[def-hilbert-direct-sum-of-unitary-representations]]). If $(\varepsilon,s_0)\ne(1,0)$, the irreducible class $[I_{\varepsilon,is_0}]$ lies in the Fell closure of $S_{\varepsilon,s_0,\delta}$; at $(\varepsilon,s_0)=(1,0)$, the reducible $I_{1,0}=D_1^+\oplus D_1^-$ is not a point of $\widehat G$, but both irreducible summands $D_1^+$ and $D_1^-$ lie in the Fell closure of $S_{1,0,\delta}$ ([[def-fell-topology-on-the-unitary-dual]], [[def-unitary-dual-of-a-locally-compact-group]], [[def-limits-of-discrete-series-for-sl2-r]], [[thm-unitarity-and-irreducibility-of-the-limits-of-discrete-series]]).
items.strategy: Write the normalized principal-series parameter as $is$ with real spectral parameter $s$. On $K\times Q$, the compact-picture cocycle $a(k,g)$ is positive continuous and hence has bounded $a$ and $|\log a|$. The identity $a^{1+is}=a e^{is\log a}$ gives an explicit uniform L2 bound for every K-finite vector; density of K-finite vectors and unitarity extend coefficient convergence to every vector. A nearby parameter supplies each coefficient witness for weak containment in a punctured-neighborhood direct sum. Generic irreducibility puts every nonexceptional class in the dual; at the odd zero endpoint, the two irreducible limits from the limits theorem are subrepresentations and inherit the same weak containment. The full reducible endpoint is not a point of the dual. The direct compact-uniform estimate is proved locally; cited sources support the compact-picture model and unitary parameter convention.

items.title: The unitary dual of SL2(R) is non-discrete and non-Hausdorff at the stated limits
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and use the Fell topology on the unitary dual of $G=\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb R)$ ([[def-fell-topology-on-the-unitary-dual]], [[def-unitary-dual-of-a-locally-compact-group]]).

**(1)** As $s\downarrow0$ through positive values, the classes $[I_{1,is}]$ converge to both distinct classes $[D_1^-]$ and $[D_1^+]$. Consequently the unitary dual is not Hausdorff.

**(2)** As $s\downarrow0$ through positive values, the pairwise distinct classes $[I_{0,is}]$ converge to $[I_{0,0}]$. Consequently the unitary dual is not discrete.

**(3)** For $0<r<1$, the spherical complementary classes $[I_{0,r}]$ are distinct from the trivial class and converge to it as $r\uparrow1$, as in [[cor-complementary-series-converge-to-the-trivial-representation]].

The same positive-parameter sequence then converges in the Fell topology to both limits; distinct K-type supports show the limits differ. (2) Use the same coefficient continuity for the even family. Restrict to s>0, since the original all-nonzero-parameter assertion double-counted sign-equivalent classes; the Casimir scalar distinguishes any two positive s and separates them from I_{0,0}. (3) Invoke the assigned complementary-series convergence corollary, whose unitary input remains open.

items.title: Lowest K-types of the first holomorphic discrete series
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). In the holomorphic model $D_2^-=(\pi_2,\mathcal H_2^+)$ of [[def-holomorphic-and-antiholomorphic-discrete-series-models]], put $f_{2,j}(z)=(z-i)^j(z+i)^{-2-j}$. The extremal vector $f_{2,0}(z)=(z+i)^{-2}$ has norm squared $\pi/4$, so $(2/\sqrt\pi)f_{2,0}$ has unit norm; it is annihilated by $L_{E_+}$ and has K-character $e^{-2i\theta}$. The vectors $f_{2,j}$, $j\ge0$, form the complete multiplicity-one K-type chain with characters $e^{-i(2+2j)\theta}$; their ladder coefficients are $L_{E_+}f_{2,0}=0$, $L_{E_+}f_{2,j}=-j f_{2,j-1}$ for $j\ge1$, and $L_{E_-}f_{2,j}=(2+j)f_{2,j+1}$ for $j\ge0$.
items.strategy: At $n=2$, $y^{n-2}=1$ and $|z+i|^2=x^2+(y+1)^2$. Tonelli and the substitution $x=(y+1)\tan t$ give $\int_{\mathbb R}(x^2+(y+1)^2)^{-2}dx=\pi/(2(y+1)^3)$, so the remaining $y$-integral is $\pi/4$ and $2f_{2,0}/\sqrt\pi$ is normalized. The model supplies the K-character and exact ladder formulas; the weighted Hilbert-space supplier gives the complete orthogonal K-type basis and the discrete-series theorem supplies irreducibility. The direct $n=2$ integrations and ladder substitutions use no further choice.

items.title: Weighted norm invariance for the inversion generator
items.statement:
For $w=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\-1&0\end{pmatrix}\in K$, one has $w\cdot z=-1/z$ and $j(w^{-1},z)=z$. Thus at $n=2$,
$$\pi_2(w)f(z)=z^{-2}f(-1/z)=(-z)^{-2}f(-1/z).$$
For every $f\in\mathcal H_2^+$ this is a bijective isometry of $\mathcal H_2^+$; explicitly, substituting $z=-1/u$ in its squared norm cancels the factor $|u|^4$ from $|z|^{-4}$ against the real Jacobian $|u|^{-4}$.
items.strategy: Set z=-1/u, compute the Jacobian |u|^{-4}, and combine it with the automorphy multiplier |z|^{-4}=|u|^4 in the n=2 norm. The global nonnegative change-of-variables theorem handles the entire upper half-plane. The group relation w²=-I shows the isometry is onto.

items.title: A square-integrable discrete-series matrix coefficient
items.statement: For $D_2^-$, let $u_2$ be the normalized extremal K-vector from [[lem-k-type-coefficient-formulas-for-the-sl2-discrete-and-principal-series]]. Its coefficient $c_2(g)=\langle\pi_2(g)u_2,u_2\rangle$ satisfies $c_2(a_\tau)=\operatorname{sech}^2(\tau/2)$ and has exact squared norm $\int_G|c_2(g)|^2dg=4\pi$ for the fixed left Haar measure. The assigned theorem [[thm-square-integrability-of-sl2-r-discrete-series-matrix-coefficients]] supplies the broader K-finite coefficient result for $D_2^-$. At the $n=1$ limit endpoint, the compact-picture weight-one coefficient $c_1(a_\tau)=\operatorname{sech}(\tau/2)$ instead has infinite squared integral.
items.strategy: Use the assigned normalized-coefficient formula for the n=2 extremal K-vector. Its modulus is K-bi-invariant, so the exact KAK formula gives a radial integral; substituting u=tanh(tau/2) evaluates it to 4π. The square-integrability theorem supplies the broader K-finite claim. At n=1, use the assigned compact-picture coefficient and the same KAK measure; the tail integrand is bounded below by 1, so monotone convergence proves divergence.

items.title: A limit of discrete series is not square-integrable
items.statement: The claim that every limit of discrete series is square-integrable in the all-matrix-coefficients sense of [[thm-the-limits-of-discrete-series-are-not-square-integrable]] is false. In the fixed Haar normalization of [[def-left-haar-integral-and-left-haar-measure]] and [[lem-kak-integration-formula-for-k-bi-invariant-functions-on-sl2-r]], the limit $D_1^+$ has a unit matrix coefficient whose squared modulus has infinite integral. By contrast, for each genuine discrete-series parameter $n\ge2$, the corresponding normalized extremal coefficient has finite squared integral.
items.strategy: Use the unit weight vector in the compact-picture limit D_1^+ and its locally authored coefficient formula. KAK turns its squared coefficient into 2 tanh(tau/2), whose positive lower bound on the tail forces an infinite integral by monotone convergence. For n≥2, the normalized discrete-series extremal coefficient gives the finite comparison integral 4π/(n−1). The cited sources and current in-run suppliers do not substitute for these local calculations.

items.title: Parameter identifications in the SL2(R) unitary dual
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and use the normalized parameter $I_{\varepsilon,
u}$ and exceptional lattice $\mathcal W_\varepsilon$ of [[def-normalized-principal-series-i-epsilon-nu]]. The following records the parameter identifications and reducible endpoints in this normalization.

For $
u
otin\mathcal W_\varepsilon$, the irreducible principal-series representations satisfy $I_{\varepsilon,
u}\cong I_{\varepsilon,-
u}$. For nonzero $
u\in\mathcal W_\varepsilon$, the two reducible full induced modules are not isomorphic. At $\varepsilon=1,
u=0$, one has $I_{1,0}=D_1^-\oplus D_1^+$.

The K-types of $I_{\varepsilon,
u}$ are exactly the characters of parity $m\equiv\varepsilon\pmod2$, each with multiplicity one. If $n\in\mathcal W_\varepsilon$ and $n\ge1$, then at $
u=n$ the composition factors are $L_{n-1}$ and the two extremal modules $M^-_{n+1},M^+_{-(n+1)}$, with $L_{n-1}$ the quotient; at $
u=-n$ the finite-dimensional factor is the submodule and the two tails form the quotient. For $n\ge2$, the discrete series $D_n^-$ and $D_n^+$ are the modules $M^+_{-n}$ and $M^-_n$, respectively, at $
u=n-1$. At $\varepsilon=0,
u=\pm1$, the trivial module $L_0$ is a subquotient.

The unitary principal-series parameters are $I_{0,is}$ for $s\ge0$ and $I_{1,is}$ for $s>0$; the even point $I_{0,0}$ is irreducible, while $I_{1,0}$ is the limit split above. The spherical complementary family has parameters $I_{0,r}$ for $0<r<1$, with the sign labels $r$ and $-r$ identified; $
u=\pm1$ are degenerate endpoints, not additional irreducible complementary-series points. Within each principal or complementary family, no two different absolute parameter values give isomorphic representations.
items.strategy: Record the sign equivalence and nonisomorphism at exceptional parameters from [[thm-equivalence-i-epsilon-nu-is-i-epsilon-minus-nu]], then compile the K-type parity, exceptional composition factors, limit split, and discrete-series model identifications from their exact A-page suppliers. The compact-picture theorem supplies the imaginary principal unitary axis. The spherical complementary range is retained as a flagged open input because the assigned batch-3 item file is absent. Compare central scalars and K-type supports to distinguish the unitary principal and complementary parameter families; exceptional full induced modules are reducible and are not counted as additional dual points.
